senses.gloss: m. (campus, κάμπος, accus.) plain for exercise and amusement.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 23:2">Kel. XXIII, 2</cite> <he>מפני שעומדין עליו בקמ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>בקומ׳</he>; Ar. s. v. <he>קנפון</he>: <he>בקנפון</he>) because soldiers at sports stand on it. Pesik. B’shall. 82ᵇ <he>כל עמא יפקון לק׳</he> let all people go out to the campus (for public court); <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:14:2">Cant. R. to II, 14</cite>; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 6">Lev. R. s. 6</cite>.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 31:4">Lev. R. s. 31</cite> <he>יהו מחזירין אותו בק׳</he> they shall make him go around in the campus (for public disgrace); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 810">Yalk. Deut. 810</cite>; <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite> Ar. Var. <he>קנ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P01184"><he>עֲקִיפִים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 21:1">Pesik. R. s. 21</cite> <he>מלך … בקימ׳</he> (corr. acc.) a king going out to the plain for sport, opp. <he>יוצא למלחמה</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 24:1">Kel. XXIV, 1</cite> <he>שמשחקין בו בקוּנְפּוֹן</he> (Ar. <he>בקנ׳</he>; Hai G. <he>בקופ׳</he>, corr. acc.) with which they play in the field; a. fr.
